overview.heading: How the Sticker Maker works
paragraphs: You describe the sticker in a sentence, optionally add a few words of text, and pick one of ten art styles. PiCraft draws a single centered design with a thick white die-cut border, then removes the backdrop so the PNG is transparent everywhere outside that border.

The transparent edge is what a cutting machine or a sticker printer follows. Because the white border sits just inside that edge, a small cutting error shows up as a little extra white instead of a sliver of missing artwork.
Each generation uses one credit and produces a fresh design, so you can try the same idea in several styles and keep the one you like best.

whatYouGet.title: Transparent 2048×2048 PNG
whatYouGet.description: The full-size file with the background removed. It holds up for stickers around 6 inches across at 300 DPI and gives you room to edit in your own software.

whatYouGet.title: 3×3 inch print file
whatYouGet.description: A 900×900 px PNG at 300 DPI, sized for the most common sticker format and ready to place on a sheet or in Cricut Design Space.

whatYouGet.title: A built-in white border
whatYouGet.description: Every design is outlined with a continuous white border, the classic die-cut look and an easy cut path for machines and printers to follow.

whatYouGet.title: Ten art styles
whatYouGet.description: From kawaii and cartoon to pixel art, woodcut and neon glow, so one idea can become a whole pack with different personalities.

whatYouGet.title: Optional text
whatYouGet.description: Add a short phrase of up to 30 characters and it is drawn into the design as part of the artwork, spelled the way you typed it.

useCases.title: Etsy and Redbubble shops
useCases.description: Test a niche quickly by making several designs around one keyword, then list the ones that look best. Each file is already transparent, so it can go straight into a listing or a print-on-demand upload.

useCases.title: Cricut and Silhouette Print Then Cut
useCases.description: Upload the PNG, save it as a Print Then Cut image, print it on sticker paper and let the machine cut around the white border.

useCases.title: Planners and journals
useCases.description: Make small themed stickers for habit trackers, study notes or bullet journals: a tired cat for Monday, a tiny plant for water reminders.

useCases.title: Packaging and thank-you stickers
useCases.description: Seal order bags with a custom character or a short thank-you line. Small shops use them to make a plain mailer feel branded.

useCases.title: Classrooms, parties and gifts
useCases.description: Reward stickers, party favors and name tags are quick to make when you can describe the idea in one line and print at home. To start from a photo of a person or a pet instead of a text idea, the [photo sticker sheet](/create/photo-trend-maker/photo-sticker-sheet) look makes nine stickers on one flat picture.

tips.title: Describe one subject, not a scene
tips.description: A single character or object reads clearly at 3 inches. Crowded scenes lose detail once printed small.

tips.title: Say what the subject is doing
tips.description: "A sleepy cat curled up inside a coffee mug" gives the model a pose and a silhouette. "Cat" produces something generic.

tips.title: Keep text to a few words
tips.description: One to four words work best. Long phrases get cramped and are more likely to contain a letter that is off, so proofread whatever you add.

tips.title: Match the style to the subject
tips.description: Kawaii suits animals and food, woodcut suits landscapes and creatures, pop art suits loud one-liners. If a result feels flat, switch the style before rewriting the idea.

tips.title: Avoid trademarked characters and logos
tips.description: Describe an original idea instead of a known cartoon or brand. Marketplaces remove listings that copy other people's characters.

tips.title: Generate two or three variations
tips.description: Every generation is a new design. Running the same idea in a couple of styles is the fastest way to find the one worth printing.

tips.title: Check the edge on a dark background
tips.description: Open the PNG over a dark color in your editor. A continuous white border and no leftover grey fringe means it is ready to cut.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing a sticker style
styleGuide.intro: Each style changes the line work, palette and mood of the design. Use this as a quick guide to which one fits your idea.

items.title: Cute kawaii
items.description: Soft pastels, round shapes and happy faces. Best for animals, food and gifts.

items.title: Bold cartoon
items.description: Thick outlines and flat bright colors. Best for mascots, memes and anything that must read from a distance.

items.title: Retro 70s
items.description: Warm orange, mustard and brown with groovy shapes. Best for [travel, music and nostalgic slogans](/create/sticker-maker/retro).

items.title: Watercolor
items.description: Gentle washes with fine ink details. Best for flowers, nature and journal stickers.

items.title: Pixel art
items.description: Crisp 16-bit look with a limited palette. Best for gaming, tech and developer humor.

items.title: Chibi anime
items.description: Big heads, tiny bodies and sparkly eyes. Best for characters and fandom-style art.

items.title: Hand-drawn doodle
items.description: Loose pen lines with minimal color. Best for quick jokes and minimalist packs.

items.title: Neon glow
items.description: Electric colors with glowing edges. Best for nightlife, music and bold statements.

items.title: Pop art
items.description: Halftone dots, primary colors and heavy outlines. Best for punchy phrases and comic-style scenes.

items.title: Woodcut print
items.description: Carved black lines with limited flat color. Best for [wildlife, outdoors and craft brands](/create/sticker-maker/woodcut).

checklist.heading: Before you print or sell
items: Zoom in on the PNG over a dark background and confirm the white border is continuous.
Read any text letter by letter. A single wrong character is easy to miss on screen and obvious on paper.
Print one test sticker on plain paper to confirm the size and the look.
Set the print scale to 100% so the 300 DPI file is not stretched or shrunk by your software.
In Cricut Design Space, save the upload as a Print Then Cut image and check that the cut preview follows the white border.
Make sure the design contains no trademarked characters, logos or brand names.
Use waterproof vinyl or add a laminate layer for stickers that will be handled, washed or left outdoors.

limits: The result is a flat image, not layers. To change something, generate again with a new description.
Very pale grey areas that touch the edge of the image can be lost when the background is removed. Regenerate if that happens.
Each generation is one sticker, not a laid-out sheet. Place several PNGs on a page in your print software.
Cut lines are not included. The transparent edge is the cut path, and you set up cutting in your machine's software.
Text beyond a few words can come out garbled, so always proofread.
